subject: environmental-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Within the pollution-management model, intervening at the level of the 'process of production' (e.g. redesigning to use cleaner technology) is generally preferable to cleaning up released pollutants because it:
options: Shifts the cost onto third parties
Removes the need for any monitoring
Is always cheaper in the short term
Prevents the pollutant being produced or released in the first place
questions.explain: The pollution-management model favours prevention at source over end-of-pipe treatment, since avoiding release is usually more effective and less costly than later clean-up.

questions.q: Which catalytic-converter outcome reduces vehicle emissions of nitrogen oxides?
options: Reducing NOx back to nitrogen and oxygen
Trapping particulates in a filter
Oxidising CO to CO2
Converting unburnt hydrocarbons to water
questions.explain: A three-way catalytic converter reduces NOx to nitrogen and oxygen while oxidising CO and hydrocarbons.

questions.q: Which of the following is classified as an INORGANIC pollutant?
options: Untreated sewage
Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)
Crude oil
Heavy metals such as lead and mercury
questions.explain: Toxic heavy metals like lead, mercury and cadmium are inorganic pollutants, whereas oil, PCBs and sewage are organic in nature.

questions.q: Stratospheric ozone (O3) is naturally formed when ultraviolet light splits which molecule?
options: Water vapour
Molecular oxygen (O2)
Carbon dioxide
Nitrogen (N2)
questions.explain: UV radiation photodissociates O2 into oxygen atoms, which then combine with O2 to form ozone (O3).

questions.q: In which atmospheric layer is the ozone layer that absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation concentrated?
options: Mesosphere
Stratosphere
Thermosphere
Troposphere
questions.explain: The protective ozone layer lies in the stratosphere, where it absorbs much of the Sun's UV-B and UV-C radiation.

questions.q: Bioaccumulation differs from biomagnification in that bioaccumulation specifically describes:
options: The breakdown of a pollutant by decomposers
The dilution of a pollutant in water
The increase in pollutant concentration between trophic levels
The build-up of a pollutant within a single organism over its lifetime
questions.explain: Bioaccumulation is the gradual build-up of a substance within one organism over time, whereas biomagnification compares concentrations across successive trophic levels.

questions.q: Eutrophication of a lake following nutrient pollution typically leads to:
options: Increased dissolved oxygen and greater fish diversity
A fall in primary productivity
Algal blooms, subsequent decomposition, oxygen depletion and fish kills
Permanent clearing of the water column
questions.explain: Excess nitrate and phosphate trigger algal blooms; when the algae die, their decomposition by bacteria depletes dissolved oxygen, killing fish and other aerobic life.

questions.q: Fitting flue-gas desulfurisation (scrubbers) to a coal power station is an example of pollution management at which level?
options: Changing consumer attitudes
Altering the human activity producing the pollutant
Controlling the release of the pollutant
Cleaning up and restoring the damaged system
questions.explain: Scrubbers reduce SO2 once it is produced but before release, which is the 'controlling release' level of the pollution-management model.

questions.q: Light pollution is an environmental concern mainly because it:
options: Raises atmospheric carbon dioxide
Disrupts the behaviour and navigation of nocturnal and migratory species
Depletes stratospheric ozone
Acidifies rainfall
questions.explain: Artificial night-time lighting disrupts circadian rhythms, breeding, foraging and migration in many animals such as turtles, birds and insects.

questions.q: Mercury entering aquatic food webs is especially hazardous to humans because micro-organisms convert it into:
options: Insoluble mercury sulfide that sinks harmlessly
Mercuric oxide that is rapidly excreted
Elemental mercury vapour that escapes to air
Methylmercury, a fat-soluble form that biomagnifies
questions.explain: Bacteria convert inorganic mercury into methylmercury, which is lipid-soluble, biomagnifies up food chains and damages the human nervous system.

questions.q: Which of the following is a SECONDARY pollutant rather than a primary pollutant?
options: Ground-level (tropospheric) ozone
Carbon monoxide from a car exhaust
Sulfur dioxide emitted from a power station
Particulate soot from combustion
questions.explain: Ground-level ozone is a secondary pollutant formed by reactions of primary pollutants in sunlight, not emitted directly.

questions.q: Which statement about the atmosphere's vertical temperature profile is correct?
options: Temperature only changes in the thermosphere
Temperature is constant throughout all layers
Temperature rises continuously from the surface upward
Temperature falls with altitude in the troposphere but rises in the stratosphere
questions.explain: Temperature decreases with height in the troposphere then increases in the stratosphere due to ozone absorbing UV.

questions.q: Which gas is the most abundant by volume in Earth's dry atmosphere?
options: Nitrogen
Oxygen
Argon
Carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the dry atmosphere by volume, far more than oxygen at around 21%.

questions.q: Which pair of gases is most directly responsible for acid deposition?
options: SO2 and NOx
N2 and O2
O3 and CFCs
CO2 and CH4
questions.explain: Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides react with water in the atmosphere to form sulfuric and nitric acids.

questions.q: Adding powdered limestone to an acidified lake to raise its pH is an example of:
options: Altering human activity
Preventing the pollutant from forming
Controlling the release of pollutants
Restoring the damaged ecosystem
questions.explain: Liming neutralises acidity after damage has occurred, which is the clean-up/restoration level of pollution management.

questions.q: A 'persistent' pollutant is one that:
options: Has no toxic effects on living organisms
Breaks down rapidly into harmless products
Is only ever released from point sources
Resists breakdown and remains in the environment for a long time
questions.explain: Persistent pollutants such as DDT and many plastics resist degradation and therefore accumulate in the environment and food chains over time.

questions.q: How do chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) destroy stratospheric ozone?
options: They cool the stratosphere so ozone condenses
They absorb ozone directly without reacting
UV radiation releases chlorine atoms that catalytically break down ozone
They react with oxygen to prevent ozone forming
questions.explain: UV light frees chlorine radicals from CFCs, and each chlorine atom can catalytically destroy thousands of ozone molecules.

questions.q: Which describes 'dry deposition' of acidifying pollutants?
options: Acid neutralised by limestone before deposition
Acids dissolved in rain, snow and fog
Acid formed only inside cloud droplets
Gases and particles settling directly onto surfaces without precipitation
questions.explain: Dry deposition is the direct settling of acidic gases and particles onto surfaces, distinct from wet deposition in precipitation.

questions.q: Fine particulate matter classified as PM2.5 is a health concern mainly because it:
options: Is too large to be inhaled
Reflects sunlight back to space
Only affects plant leaves
Penetrates deep into the lungs and bloodstream
questions.explain: PM2.5 particles are small enough to reach the alveoli and enter the bloodstream, causing respiratory and cardiovascular harm.

questions.q: Biomagnification refers to the process by which:
options: The concentration of a persistent pollutant increases at successive trophic levels
A pollutant is diluted as it moves up the food chain
Nutrients become more abundant in producers
A pollutant breaks down faster inside organisms
questions.explain: Biomagnification is the increasing concentration of a persistent, fat-soluble pollutant in organisms at higher trophic levels of a food chain.

questions.q: A key advantage of using biotic indices over a single direct chemical measurement to assess river pollution is that biotic indices:
options: Reflect conditions integrated over time rather than a single instant
Are cheaper but ignore biological effects
Cannot detect intermittent pollution events
Require expensive laboratory equipment for every sample
questions.explain: Living organisms integrate exposure over time, so biotic indices can reveal intermittent or past pollution that a one-off chemical 'snapshot' might miss.

questions.q: The 'hole' in the ozone layer is most pronounced over which region?
options: The equator
Antarctica in spring
The mid-latitudes year round
The Arctic only
questions.explain: Polar stratospheric clouds over Antarctica in spring promote chlorine-catalysed ozone destruction, creating the seasonal ozone hole.

questions.q: Acid deposition can damage forests indirectly by:
options: Adding excess nitrogen that all plants need
Increasing soil pH and locking nutrients
Coating leaves in a protective wax
Mobilising toxic aluminium ions and leaching nutrients from soils
questions.explain: Acidified soils release toxic aluminium and leach away calcium and magnesium, harming roots and reducing nutrient uptake.

questions.q: Microplastics are usually defined as plastic particles that are:
options: Always manufactured deliberately as microbeads
Biodegradable within weeks
Larger than 5 cm
Less than 5 mm in diameter
questions.explain: Microplastics are plastic fragments smaller than 5 mm, arising both from manufactured microbeads and from the breakdown of larger plastic items.

questions.q: Liming lakes treats the symptoms of acid deposition but not the cause because it:
options: Removes SO2 from power station emissions
Neutralises acidity without reducing emissions of acidifying gases
Stops cars from emitting NOx
Prevents acid forming in clouds
questions.explain: Liming only restores damaged water bodies; emissions of SO2 and NOx continue unless tackled at source.

questions.q: Plastic pollution harms marine animals such as turtles and seabirds primarily through:
options: Increasing water salinity
Raising sea temperature
Ingestion and entanglement
Lowering ocean pH directly
questions.explain: Marine animals mistake plastic for food (ingestion) and become trapped in debris such as nets and rings (entanglement), causing injury and death.

questions.q: Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) such as PCBs and dioxins are of particular concern because they are:
options: Confined to the atmosphere only
Persistent, fat-soluble and prone to biomagnification
Naturally occurring and harmless
Water-soluble and rapidly excreted
questions.explain: POPs resist degradation, dissolve in fats and biomagnify up food chains, so they accumulate in top predators and humans, prompting controls such as the Stockholm Convention.

questions.q: The 'LD50' of a toxic substance is the dose that:
options: Halves the substance's half-life
Causes a 50% reduction in body mass
Is lethal to 50% of a test population
Produces no observable effect in 50% of subjects
questions.explain: LD50 (median lethal dose) is the dose that kills 50% of a test population, providing a standard comparative measure of acute toxicity.

questions.q: One reason the Montreal Protocol is considered highly successful is that it:
options: Banned all fossil fuel use
Achieved near-universal ratification and measurable ozone recovery
Required no replacement chemicals
Eliminated all greenhouse gas emissions
questions.explain: Its broad adoption and phase-out of ODS have allowed stratospheric ozone to begin recovering.

questions.q: Thermal pollution of a river by a power station's cooling water harms aquatic life mainly because warmer water:
options: Contains more nutrients
Holds more dissolved oxygen
Holds less dissolved oxygen, stressing aquatic organisms
Increases the river's flow rate
questions.explain: Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen while also raising organisms' metabolic oxygen demand, so thermal pollution can cause oxygen stress and death.
